description.narrative: Syftet med insatsen är att civilsamhällets intressen ska tas till vara vid fredsförhandlingarna i Géneve. NOREF är avtalsparten.
The purpose of this contribution is to support civil society to be included in the peace negotiations in Geneva.

The purpose of this contribution is to maintain activities of the dialogue platform for Syrian Civil Society Organisations and networks to participate in the UN-facilitated peace talks for Syria. The Civil Society Support Room (CSSR) is led by the UN's Special Envoy to Syria, until 2023 with the support from two implementing partners, NOREF and Swisspeace. This contribution has supported the CSSR through NOREF from October 2017 to May 2023. The CSSR has an advising role to the Special Envoy whereby the CSSR members share their perspectives and comments which are intended to feed into the peace negotiations.
The concrete objectives as formulated for the last phase of the contribution, from 1 January 2022 to 31 May 2023, are the following:
Outcome 1 - Participation and Ownership: Ensuring the continued inclusion of a diverse range of civil society in the political process through engagement in the CSSR and strengthening Syrian ownership of the CSSR structure.
Outcome 2 - Meaningful Engagement: Ensuring that the CSSR offers civil society actors' spaces for meaningful engagement and substantive discussions, presenting ideas and recommendations that can be solicited to support the political process, including the constitution-making process.
Outcome 3 - Dialogue and Advocacy: Providing a space for dialogue and trust building among Syrian civil society actors and a platform for advocacy with key international actors.
Outcome 4 - Knowledge Generation and Management: Maintaining and developing the innovative CSSR website and online platform, with the purpose of enhancing transparency and collaboration among civil society actors. Introduction of a data analytical tool to provide better mappings and analyses.
Outcome 5 - Crosscutting Gender Mainstreaming: Ensuring that women who have received capacity building training are systematically included in all CSSR activities and considering women's interests and concerns in activity planning and thematic discussions seeking to ensure gender responsive outputs.

When analysing the results over the entire seven year period of the contribution, NOREF highlights that the CSSR has been instrumental in civil society being formalised as a peace actor in the UN Syria process. Also in periods of less activity in the political arena, the civil society has remained a partner in the UN Syria Process through the CSSR. The importance of the CSSR is according to NOREF indicated in how the UN Special Envoy (UNSE) over time increasingly has explicitly referred to the CSSR in briefings to the UN Security Council.
CSSR has according to NOREF's analysis been instrumental in demonstrating the importance of a multitrack approach, enabling local peace building and dialogue initiatives to connect with Track 2 and Track 3. There was also a certain overlap of participants in the CSSR and other formal and informal tracks, which further facilitated the exchange of thoughts and experiences among different levels of peacebuilding initiatives. The CSSR network was consulted when the Constitutional Committee (CC) was set up, and civil society was represented through participants to the Middle Third within the CC. The Civil Society could thus gain a more pronounced role within the constitutional talks. Furthermore, NOREF assesses that the Syrian civil society through the CSSR may have gained a greater preparedness to engage in any future national dialogue process.
NOREF also highlights that the CSSR has contributed to building trust and dialogue among the Syrian civil society. Through the CSSR, Syrians from different parts of Syria and the diaspora, as well as from different contexts and political backgrounds, have had their own platform for dialogue, which has also led to their own advocacy efforts. The Brussels Conference has been one arena for such advocacy. An LSE study published in 2019 found that "eighty-one per cent of respondents... reported that CSSR participation helped to break barriers and converge conflicting viewpoints" (Turkmani and Theros: "A process in its own right: the Syrian Civil Society Support Room".) It should be noted that the CSSR, having been the subject of studies and reviews, has also contributed to further knowledge about inclusion in peacebuilding and mediation processes.
Between 2021 and 2023, the CSSR has worked in Thematic Working Groups, which has enabled the participants to address issues related to UNSCR 2254 which are not directly linked to the constitutional process. The Thematic Working Groups were established to strengthen dialogue and Syrian ownership of the CSSR. The fact that the Thematic Working Groups mainly met virtually, although IRL meetings in Geneva have also occurred, facilitated for participants to engage regardless of their geographical area. This transition to a virtual platform was initially a response to Covid-19, but has continued beyond the pandemic. Examples of themes explored in the Thematic Working Groups are Protection and Humanitarian access, and Local Governance and Decentralisation. Through the Thematic Working Groups, the CSSR has been able to provide insights and ideas to the UN-OSE on a broad range of issues relevant to different aspects of the UN mediation efforts.
NOREF and Swisspeace have also worked to enhance the skills of Syrian women peacebuilders within the framework of the CSSR. During the 2021 pilot phase, 23 Syrian women participated in training covering e.g. mediation, advocacy, facilitation and communication. Three of the participants were also engaged in the Constitutional Committee. Some of the participating women in their turn conducted training for other women in their communities. According to NOREF, those trained increased their engagement in the CSSR, and were more likely to take on additional roles and responsibility within the platform.
The training initiative continued for a short time beyond the pilot phase, with three additional trainings. However, it should be noted that the CSSR has continuously strived to engage women, with invitation lists generally aimed at being balanced 50 50 between men and women. Furthermore, from 2022, the focus on the inclusion of youth increased, both in terms of outreach to youth and the integration of Syrian youth perspectives.
